Fosforun emilimi kaynağına göre değişir::
How well phosphorus is absorbed depends on where it comes from:

• Plant phosphorus (legumes, grains): absorbed least (bound as phytate).
• Animal phosphorus (meat, milk, eggs): absorbed moderately.
• ADDITIVE phosphorus (phosphoric acid, phosphate salts): almost all of it is absorbed.

• Tomato paste and ready-made sauces
• Pickles, brined olives, pickle juice
• White cheese and tulum cheese (brined)
• Sucuk, salami, pastırma, kavurma
• Instant soup, stock cubes, ready-made spice mixes
• Bread (little per portion, but it adds up over the day)
• Mineral water and soda (sodium is high in some brands)

İki diyaliz seansı arasında vücutta biri:
The fluid that builds up between two dialysis sessions shows up as a gain on the scale. The literature aims for this gain (IDWG) to be LESS than 4.0–4.5 % of dry body weight.

Example: for someone whose dry weight is 70 kg, 4 % = 2.8 kg.

Too large a gain leads to:
• High blood pressure and strain on the heart
• More aggressive ultrafiltration during the session, with the cramps and drops in blood pressure that come with it
• Shortness of breath, swelling in the legs

The main driver of the gain is not WATER but SODIUM: salty food creates thirst and holds fluid in the body. Cutting sodium gets results more easily than restricting fluid.

The fluid limit is set per patient; the same literature argues for an individual prescription rather than a fixed volume.
